original_question: Let f : X 99K X be a dominant rational map of a smooth projective variety X defined over Q̄. (a) Let P ∈ X(Q̄)f . The limit (15.6) defining αf (P ) converges. (b) The set αf (P ) : P ∈ X(Q̄)f is finite. (c) Let P ∈ X(Q̄)f . The arithmetic degree αf (P ) is an algebraic integer. (d) Let P ∈ X(Q̄)f whose orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in X. Then αf (P ) = δf . The inequality (15.7) ᾱf (P ) ≤ δf for P ∈ X(Q̄)f relating arithmetic and dynamical degrees is true in the more general setting of.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 15.9 (Arithmetic Degree Conjectures) in Section 15.1, which is the paper's verbatim generalization of Conjecture 15.3 from projective space to smooth projective varieties.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper: it reproduces almost verbatim the four clauses of Conjecture 15.9, namely existence of the limit defining alpha_f(P), finiteness of the set of arithmetic degrees, algebraic-integrality of each arithmetic degree, and equality alpha_f(P)=delta_f for points with Zariski-dense forward orbit. It also correctly references the surrounding formulas (15.6) and (15.7).
missing_details: The paper's exact target is Conjecture 15.9 in Section 15.1, not a broader open problem about all relations between arithmetic and dynamical degrees.
You need to define X(Qbar)_f as the set of points P in X(Qbar) for which the full forward orbit is well-defined, i.e. f^n(P) is defined for every n >= 0.

You need to define the arithmetic degree in the general-variety setting exactly as in Definition 15.8: choose an embedding i: X -> P^N and use the induced absolute logarithmic Weil height h on P^N, so alpha_f(P) = lim_{n->infty} h(i(f^n(P)))^(1/n).
Because your draft mentions (15.7), you also need to define the upper arithmetic degree baralpha_f(P) as the same expression with limsup in place of lim.
You need to define delta_f in the general setting as the first dynamical degree from Section 14.1, not by the projective-space degree-growth formula alone.

The formulation should state explicitly that f is a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety over Qbar; there is no additional hypothesis in the paper that f be a morphism or have degree at least 2.
The paper notes that alpha_f(P), if it exists, does not depend on the chosen embedding i, but this independence is implicit in your draft and should be clarified if the question is to be stand-alone.
The clause involving (15.7) should not be presented as part of the conjecture itself: the paper explicitly says the inequality baralpha_f(P) <= delta_f is already true in this generality.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth projective variety over Qbar, let f: X dashrightarrow X be a dominant rational self-map, and let X(Qbar)_f := {P in X(Qbar) : f^n(P) is defined for every n >= 0}. Fix an embedding i: X -> P^N, let h be the absolute logarithmic Weil height on P^N, and for P in X(Qbar)_f define the arithmetic degree by alpha_f(P) := lim_{n->infty} h(i(f^n(P)))^(1/n) when the limit exists; let delta_f denote the first dynamical degree of f. Is it true that: (i) alpha_f(P) exists for every P in X(Qbar)_f; (ii) the set {alpha_f(P) : P in X(Qbar)_f} is finite; (iii) each alpha_f(P) is an algebraic integer; and (iv) if the forward orbit O_f(P) is Zariski dense in X, then alpha_f(P) = delta_f?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 15.1. Its four substatements match Conjecture 15.9 essentially word for word. The immediately preceding Definition 15.8 supplies the missing general-variety definition of alpha_f(P), while Section 14.1 supplies the correct general definition of delta_f. The only substantive correction is that the sentence about (15.7) is not part of the conjecture: the paper explicitly states that baralpha_f(P) <= delta_f is already known for dominant rational maps on smooth projective varieties. The refined version therefore sharpens the draft into the paper's actual stand-alone conjectural question without broadening it.
